Lead Paint Testing and Inspection for Milwaukee Homes

Is that peeling paint on a Milwaukee porch or window actually lead? Color and age cannot tell you. Testing can, surface by surface.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

What testing can tell you

An inspector may use an XRF instrument or collect paint samples for a laboratory. Either way, the result is a list of components, such as window sashes, door casings, porch rails and trim, marked as lead-based paint or not. That list is what makes later decisions practical.

Milwaukee has a lot of duplexes, upper-lower flats and cottages built long before 1978, and they have usually been repainted many times. A fresh coat on top says nothing about what is underneath.

Inspection or risk assessment?

An inspection locates lead paint. A risk assessment looks at whether paint, dust or soil is a hazard right now. EPA explains why these are different services. If paint is chipping, window dust keeps returning or a child has had an elevated blood lead result, a risk assessment is usually the more useful first document.

Who can do the work in Wisconsin

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services says lead testing, inspection and risk assessment in homes built before 1978 must be done by certified people working for a certified company. Ask for the certification before you book a visit, and ask which components the report will cover.

Prepare for the visit

Gather the year the building was built, any earlier lead reports, and a list of the rooms where paint is failing or where you plan to work. For a two-unit building, say which unit and which shared areas, such as stairs and entries, are part of the request.

Common questions

Who can perform a lead paint inspection in Wisconsin?

Wisconsin requires individual and company certification for lead inspection and risk assessment work in houses built before 1978. You can ask any firm for its certification numbers.

Is a general home inspection the same as a lead inspection?

No. A general home inspection does not identify lead-based paint. A lead inspection is a separate service done by a certified inspector.

Do I need testing before a small remodel?

If the house was built before 1978 and the work disturbs painted surfaces, test or treat the paint as lead-based. Window and door work, scraping and sanding are the common triggers.

Lead Risk Assessment for Milwaukee Homes and Rentals

Intact old paint is one thing. Paint that is chipping, dust on the sills and bare soil by the foundation are another. A risk assessment sorts out which you have.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

What a risk assessment looks at

A certified risk assessor checks the condition of painted surfaces, collects dust wipe samples from floors and window areas, and may sample bare soil around the building. The report names the hazards found and the controls that would address them.

It is the right first step when dust returns to the same window, when a child has an elevated blood lead result, or when a rental owner needs to know what is actually wrong before deciding on repairs.

Milwaukee's local layer

The City of Milwaukee Health Department runs a childhood lead poisoning prevention program, and its Primary Prevention Program is aimed at making properties lead-paint safe before a child is harmed. If the Health Department has contacted you about a property, bring that paperwork to the first call so the assessment scope matches what was asked.

What comes after

The report may point to cleanup, window work, repainting with proper prep, encapsulation or full abatement. Because each of those is a different job with different rules, a written scope from the assessor makes it easier to compare proposals fairly.

Common questions

How is a risk assessment different from testing the paint?

Testing identifies lead-based paint. A risk assessment identifies hazards, meaning deteriorated paint and friction surfaces plus lead in dust and soil, and tells you what to do about them.

Do I need one if a child lives in the home?

If a child has an elevated blood lead result, or you see chipping paint or window dust in a pre-1978 home, a risk assessment is a sensible step. Your child's doctor and the Milwaukee Health Department can advise on the health side.

Does it fix anything?

No. It is an investigation. The fixing is done by separate lead hazard reduction work, and the report tells the crew what to address.

Lead Dust and Soil Hazard Control in Milwaukee

Lead hazards often travel as dust and settle as soil. Sills, floors, porches and the strip of dirt along an old foundation are the usual places they show up.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Where the dust comes from

Opening and closing painted windows grinds paint into dust. Scraping a porch or sanding trim does the same, only faster. In a Milwaukee flat with original double-hung windows, the sills and the floor under them are the first place to check.

Soil near the house

Exterior paint weathers and flakes onto the ground. Bare soil along the foundation, under porches and by garages is where children play and where gardens often go. A risk assessor can sample these areas and tell you where bare ground needs to be covered or controlled.

Ask about clearance

Cleanup is only finished when a dust wipe test says so. Ask whoever does the work how they will confirm the result, and who will take the samples. See the page on clearance testing.

Common questions

Can I just wet-wipe the sills myself?

Regular wet cleaning helps with routine dust, but it does not fix the source, and it is not a substitute for testing when a child may be exposed. A risk assessment shows where the problem really is.

Is gardening in old-house soil a concern?

It can be, especially next to a pre-1978 painted exterior. Ask for soil sampling and use raised beds or cover bare ground where results call for it.

What happens after a renovation?

Disturbed paint leaves dust. Clearance testing after the work confirms it was cleaned up properly.

Lead Paint Removal and Abatement in Milwaukee

Abatement is the permanent fix: removing lead paint, replacing the component or enclosing it, done under containment by people certified to do it.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

What abatement means

EPA defines abatement as activity designed to permanently eliminate lead-based paint hazards. In practice that means removing the paint, replacing the component, or enclosing or sealing it in a durable way, followed by cleanup and testing.

Rules that apply in Milwaukee

In Wisconsin, lead abatement requires certified individuals and a certified company. In the city of Milwaukee, the Health Department says no one may perform lead abatement work without a lead hazard reduction project permit, and permit holders have to follow the city's site preparation and reduction standards. Ask any firm to show you both.

What a good proposal contains

Look for the rooms and components covered, the method for each, how the work area will be contained, how waste is handled, and how clearance will be done. A scope that only says "remove lead paint" leaves too much open.

Planning around a family or tenants

Families usually leave the work area during abatement. Raise relocation, access to the unit and timing in the first conversation, especially in a duplex where another household shares walls or stairs.

Common questions

Is painting over lead paint abatement?

Not by itself. Covering paint with new paint is general maintenance. Abatement permanently addresses the hazard, and it is done by certified workers.

Who does the work?

In Wisconsin it has to be a certified lead abatement contractor with certified workers. In Milwaukee the work also needs a city permit.

Does it end with clearance testing?

It should. A dust wipe clearance confirms the area was cleaned up before anyone moves back in.

Lead Paint Encapsulation and Enclosure in Milwaukee

Not every lead surface has to come out. Where the paint is sound and the surface is right, a durable coating or a physical barrier can control the hazard.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Two different approaches

Encapsulation applies a specialized coating that bonds to the paint and seals it in. Enclosure installs a durable barrier, such as new siding, panels or trim covering, so the lead paint is no longer exposed. Both count as lead hazard reduction when done correctly.

When it fits

The surface needs to be in sound condition. Paint that is flaking off in sheets, or a component that rubs and makes dust, such as an old sash, is rarely a good candidate. A risk assessor can say which components could be treated this way and which should be replaced.

Keep it from becoming a repaint

Ordinary paint is not encapsulation. Ask for the product name and the method, and confirm the work is done by certified people in a pre-1978 home. Ask also how the sealed surfaces will be monitored over time.

Common questions

Is encapsulation permanent?

It lasts as long as the coating or barrier stays intact, so the surface needs to be checked over time. Removal and replacement are the options that take the lead paint out.

Can it be used on windows?

Moving parts make dust, so friction surfaces are often better handled by replacement or repair than by coating.

Do I still need testing?

Yes. Testing tells you where lead paint is and which surfaces are candidates for this method.

Lead-Safe Window and Door Replacement in Milwaukee

Old wood windows open and close against painted surfaces, which is exactly how lead dust gets made. Replacing the worst offenders can take the problem out of daily life.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Why windows come up so often

A double-hung sash rubs against its frame every time it moves. Doors do the same at the jamb and threshold. In a house with lead paint, that friction puts dust on the sill and the floor, right where small children crawl and play.

Renovation or abatement?

The method matters. Replacement done as a paid renovation in a pre-1978 home falls under Wisconsin lead-safe renovation requirements, which include certified renovators and lead-safe work practices. Replacement done as a planned hazard reduction project follows the abatement rules instead. The proposal should say which one you are getting.

Plan around the neighborhood

Milwaukee has many older neighborhoods where original windows are part of the look. If your building is in a historic district, ask the city what review is required before replacing windows, and plan lead-safe work and approvals together.

Common questions

Do I have to replace every window?

Not necessarily. A risk assessment can identify the components that create the most dust and the ones that can be treated another way.

Who should do the work?

In Wisconsin, paid window replacement in a pre-1978 home needs a certified renovator or a certified abatement contractor, depending on the project.

Is cleanup part of the job?

It should be. Ask how the area will be cleaned and verified once the new window is in.

Lead Clearance Testing in Milwaukee

Clearance testing is the last step: a dust wipe test that shows the work area is clean enough for people to return.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

What it is

After lead hazard work, a certified professional collects dust wipe samples from floors, sills and other surfaces in the work area and sends them to a laboratory. The results are compared to the clearance standards that apply to the project.

Why it matters

Wisconsin's DHS lists post-renovation and post-abatement clearance, including dust wipe sampling, among the activities that require certification. A visual check can miss fine dust, which is the part that gets into children's hands and mouths.

Who should take the samples

Where possible, the person doing the sampling should be independent of the crew that did the work. Ask who will collect the samples, which rooms will be tested, and what happens if the results do not pass.

Common questions

When is clearance needed?

After abatement, and in many cases after lead hazard reduction or renovation work that disturbed paint. Your scope or the agency involved will say what applies.

What if the area fails?

The area is recleaned and retested until it passes.

Can the contractor test their own work?

It is better to have an independent certified professional take the samples. At minimum, ask who is certified to do it.

Peeling Paint or Window Dust? What to Do in an Older Milwaukee Home

You see chipped paint on a porch or a gray film on a windowsill and wonder if it is lead. Here is how to think about it before you scrape, sweep or call anyone.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Do not dry-scrape or sweep it up

Dry scraping, sanding and sweeping spread fine particles. If the house was built before 1978, wet-wipe loose chips with a damp paper towel, keep children and pets away, and hold off on any scraping until you know what is under the paint.

Describe where it shows up

Note the rooms and components: window sills, porch rails, door frames, stair edges. Windows and doors that rub, and exterior paint on porches and trim, are the classic spots. This description is more useful to an inspector than a general sense that the house is old.

Pick the right service

If you want to know whether paint contains lead, ask for testing and inspection. If dust keeps coming back or a child is affected, a risk assessment is the better first step. The Milwaukee Health Department can also answer questions about children's exposure.

Common questions

Is all old paint dangerous?

No. Intact paint is less of a concern than paint that chips, peels or gets ground at windows and doors. That is why condition matters as much as age.

Should I repaint it myself?

Fixing the surface without prep can make dust. In a pre-1978 home, get the paint tested first and follow lead-safe practices.

Lead Abatement vs Lead-Safe Renovation in Wisconsin

The same window or wall can be part of two very different jobs. Knowing the difference helps you ask for the right thing and read a proposal.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

Abatement permanently addresses a hazard

EPA defines abatement as activity designed to permanently eliminate lead-based paint hazards. In Wisconsin, it must be done by a certified abatement contractor, and in the city of Milwaukee a project permit applies.

Renovation changes the building

EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting program covers paid work that disturbs paint in pre-1978 homes and child-occupied facilities. Wisconsin's lead-safe renovation rule asks contractors to be trained and certified, to give owners and occupants lead-safe information first, and to follow lead-safe work practices. The goal is to do the project without making new lead dust, not to remove the hazard for good.

Put the distinction in the proposal

Ask the professional to name the project type, the certification that applies, how the area will be contained and how it will be cleaned and tested after. If a proposal blurs the two, ask for it to be rewritten.

Common questions

Is a certified renovation firm an abatement contractor?

Not automatically. These are different certifications in Wisconsin.

Which should I ask for?

Start from the purpose. If the aim is to permanently remove a known hazard, ask about abatement. If you are remodeling and want to do it safely, ask about lead-safe renovation.

How to Hire a Certified Lead Professional in Wisconsin

Lead work in a pre-1978 home needs certified people and a certified company. A few questions make it easy to check before you sign anything.

Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}

Request a call

Describe what you are seeing in the house and we will follow up. Prefer to talk? Call {{PHONE_DISPLAY}}.

For service inquiries only. If someone is in immediate danger or you suspect acute poisoning, call 911 or Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222.

What the state requires

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services requires individual and company certification for lead-based paint work in houses and child care centers built before 1978. That covers abatement, testing and risk assessment, renovations that disturb paint and clearance sampling.

Questions to ask a firm

Ask for the company's certification, the certification of the person who will visit, and which discipline it covers. Ask what the report or scope will include and who will take the clearance samples.

Check the Milwaukee layer

For abatement inside the city, the Health Department requires a lead hazard reduction project permit. Ask whether the firm holds one and who pulls it for your project.

Common questions

Can a general contractor do lead work?

Only if certified for the type of work involved. Certification is specific to the kind of lead activity.

Where can I look up certifications?

The Wisconsin DHS lead pages list certification information and training providers, and a firm should be able to show you its own certificates.

A neighborhood of multi-unit buildings

Riverwest has many older duplexes and small multi-unit buildings close to the river. In such a building, the scope of any lead work should name the units, stairs and shared entry areas.

Shared stairs and porches

Porches and back stairs get heavy use and weather quickly. They are common sources of chipping exterior paint and dust that tracks inside.

Tenants and owners

Homes with original woodwork

Washington Heights is a residential neighborhood on Milwaukee's west side with many homes from the early twentieth century. Original windows, doors and trim are part of what owners value there.

Restoring without making dust

Most of Milwaukee's housing predates the 1978 ban on lead paint, and the city's duplexes, flats and cottages have been repainted for generations. Whether you need testing, a risk assessment or abatement, we point you to the right step.

What toxic lead abatement actually covers

Most people searching for lead abatement are really trying to answer a simpler question: what do I do about this paint? A lead paint inspection finds lead paint. A risk assessment finds hazards. Abatement itself, meaning lead paint removal, replacement, enclosure or encapsulation, is the permanent fix, and clearance testing confirms the dust is gone afterward.

Milwaukee adds a local layer. The City of Milwaukee Health Department runs a childhood lead poisoning prevention program, including a Primary Prevention Program for properties, and it says abatement work in the city needs a lead hazard reduction project permit.

Wisconsin also controls who may do this work. The state Department of Health Services requires individual and company certification for lead-based paint work in homes built before 1978, so one firm may not be certified for every step.

If you do not yet know whether the paint contains lead, start with testing or inspection. If you already know lead is present and it is chipping or making dust, a risk assessment tells you what to do about it.
